title: Maternal and offspring fasting glucose and type 2 diabetes-associated genetic variants and cognitive function at age 8: a Mendelian randomization study in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children.
ehr_evidence: Extensive data have been collected from the mothers and their offspring from pregnancy onwards by questionnaire, abstraction from medical notes, record linkage and by attendance at research clinics.
summary: Mendelian randomization study investigating the causal relationship between maternal and offspring genetic risk scores for fasting glucose and type 2 diabetes and childhood cognitive function (IQ) at age 8 in the ALSPAC cohort.
key_findings: Maternal and offspring FGGRS were not associated with child IQ.
Maternal T2DGRS was positively associated with offspring IQ (mean difference 0.47, 95% CI 0.12, 0.81; p=0.01).
Offspring of mothers with diabetes/glycosuria had lower IQ scores (mean difference -3.5, 95% CI -5.6, -1.5; p=0.001).
FGGRS was strongly associated with offspring fasting glucose and HbA1c levels.
No association was found between offspring T2DGRS and child IQ.
captured_features: confounders (maternal age, education, smoking, birthweight, gestational age)
study_design: Mendelian randomization study within a prospective birth cohort
population: Mothers and offspring from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC) cohort, Bristol, England
exposure_domain: Genetic risk scores for fasting glucose and type 2 diabetes
limitations: Lack of statistical power to detect small effects
Most participants had fasting glucose and HbA1c levels within the normal range
Genetic risk scores may not fully capture the disease phenotype or environmental confounders
Associations with individual SNPs disappeared after Bonferroni correction
